items.value: COMEX gold futures lead London OTC spot: ILS about 66% after 2007 (above 80% 2002-2007); IS and CS above 90% after 2006
items.detail: Hauptfleisch, Putnins and Lucey, Journal of Futures Markets 36(6) 2016 (accepted manuscript, UTS repository). New York futures (GC) contribute more to gold price discovery than London spot. After Globex, US futures lead irrespective of market hours. Bears on whether GC is the leader of the gold underlying (it leads), not on MGC's share (MGC not studied).
items.quote: ILS tells a slightly different story. The futures market in the first year of our sample has an ILS of 66%, which rises above 80% for the years 2002 to 2007, after which it falls slightly and remains stable around 66%. ... After the move to the GLOBEX platform and introduction of international participation incentives in the futures market, intraday price discovery variation declines with US futures taking a consistent lead irrespective of market hours.

items.window: 2002-01 to 2008-12, 5-minute returns, GC SI HG futures
items.detail: Elder, Miao and Ramchander, Journal of Banking & Finance 2012 (repository version June 7, 2011; reused E.28 file). Absorption: return response mainly in 08:30-08:35 for gold and silver; copper shows a somewhat delayed response to 08:30 news; for 09:15 releases the peak R-square for gold and silver comes about 30 minutes later; for 10:00 releases a 5-10 minute delay in silver's peak; the response dissipates in less than an hour. Volatility effect decays within about 10 minutes. Authors call the response swift and the metals efficient.
items.quote: Notably, during the 8:30-8:35 minute interval, the highest adjusted R- square values are found for gold and silver. In contrast, copper exhibits a somewhat delayed response to the 8:30 announcement. For the 9:15 announcements, there is about a 30-minute delay before the realization of the highest adjusted R-square for gold and silver. ... about a 5-10 minute delay in the peak response of silver prices. In all cases, we observe that the metal prices are efficient in incorporating new economic information and the response tends to dissipate in less than an hour after the release of the announcement.

items.detail: Ma, Bouri, Xu and Zhou, 'The night effect of intraday trading: Evidence from Chinese gold and silver futures markets', Global Finance Journal 64 (2025). Peer-reviewed. Horizon 30-minute half-hours. Other venue (SHFE) of the gold and silver underlyings. Costs and out-of-sample status not in abstract. Published version of the ACFR paper in METALS-34.
items.quote: Secondly, before the launch of night trading, the first half-hour daytime returns have significant predictive power, whereas after the introduction of night trading, the first half-hour night returns become a significant predictor.

items.detail: CME whitepaper 'Leveraging CME Group Asia Trading Hours Liquidity for Cross Commodity Trading' (2023), Table 3, Wayback copy. Statistic is the AVERAGE top-of-book spread in GC ticks, not a median: all-hours average 1.39, Asia-hours average 1.37. Hourly averages range 1.31 to 1.82; over SGT 21:00-01:00 (ET 08:00-13:00 in winter, the US main session) the hourly averages are 1.35, 1.35, 1.35, 1.32, 1.31 (median 1.35; derived by work/METALS/METALS_parse_cme_wp.py, output METALS_parse_cme_wp_out.txt). MGC not measured; sibling on the same underlying. Newer than and different from METALS-1 ('one tick', 2017-18).
